column4: the plan's "CSR transpose kernel" is bound to MatCsrGraph, not to MatCsrIndex: the C refuses offsets.length != transposedOffsets.length (square adjacency) and any target >= nodes, while the module's CSR owner M3CsrIndex (PR #2499) is a rectangular row -> reference relation without a transpose; relocating MatCsrGraph would create a second CSR owner, so the kernel, its host and its oracle are NEC rows (held, blobs pinned), not FILE rows; the map gained the informational kinds NEC and OMIT

column4: the owner reads one system property (the explicit native library path) whose name carries the donor's dotted segment; NAMING_RULES.tsv rule SEGMENT_DOT renames that segment, so jdk_naming.py apply would rewrite the relocated body and break the recipe's fixed point; a declared LITERAL row (whole-token, regex-escaped) applies the same rename inside the recipe, after which jdk_naming.py plan reports 0 rewrites and relocate.py --check stays changed=0

column4: 100,000 seeded matrices with shapes up to 4,096 x 4,096 bits need bounded fills: the Builder only has set(row, column), so the dump fills dense 64 x 64 tiles (clipped at the shape), at most 4,096 sparse cells, one stride cell per 64 columns per row, and a first tile at exactly 255 or 256 bits (the probe gate), instead of setting every bit of a 16-million-bit matrix; the word lane is read through the private words field (reflection) so word-level identity, including the masked row tails, is compared, and the public surface (rowCardinality, setColumns, get) on top

the donor kernel compiles unchanged under the module's stricter CMake flags (-std=c11 -Wconversion -Wshadow -Wpedantic -Werror): every narrowing in it is an explicit cast, so no per-file compile option was needed in the registration; checked before the recipe ran (gcc on the donor bytes), then again on the relocated file

column4: the JNI parity lane of the owner (NATIVE_REQUIRED computes the Java result and compares the whole native result before publication) makes the native differential cheap to state: the reflective dump run through transpose(Backend.NATIVE_REQUIRED) must equal the Java lane dump line for line (TOTAL lines excluded, they name the backend), which it did over all 101,652 inputs for both libraries under -Xcheck:jni in about a minute each; the mutant lane (one scalar store masked to zero) is what proves the comparison is live
